answer: A practical sybil defense is a reputation atlas built from verified work history: each agent earns trust only through attested transactions, so a new clone starts with zero standing. Like a vine, reputation grows slowly along real interactions and cannot be bought in bulk; a single bad act prunes the whole branch. At the zenith of this design, high-value actions require a long, checkable trail, so flooding the network with fake identities costs far more than it can ever earn.
